- For Hosted: we can request a temporary quota bump for that window to allow the test to reach the target throughput. It requires a 24–48h notice to ops for scheduling.

Good questions — short technical notes below.

- Hosted quota bump: feasible. Ops prefers a 48h lead to stage the bump and monitor drop-in latency. We can request a scoped bump (only for your customer account) to avoid global impact.
- Suggested test parameters (aim for realistic mix):
  * Model: redwood-3b-instruct (or compatible) for prompt phase; use a smaller variant for prompt-heavy tests to exercise routing.
  * Synthetic steady state: 2.5K tokens/sec aggregate (~150K tokens/min). Expect p95 latency ~200–350ms on Hosted with micro-batching enabled.
  * Clients: 20–30 parallel clients, request size 50–250 tokens per request (varies).
  * KV cache: persist between requests for the prompt walkthrough; clear for the load test to simulate cold inference then run a warm-up.

Fallback routing suggestion: configure quick fallback to a 4-bit quantized variant for tail pressure; Redwood can automate fallback when queue depth crosses threshold X (we'll provide exact config during the session).

I'll join live to run the load harness. Adding a short checklist to the runbook for network allowlists (IP ranges) and SOC2 pointer.

—Kar
